narrativeReportMd:
# GuidanceResponse R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`GuidanceResponse` keeps the same resource identity in R6, but it has several local breaking or migration-sensitive content changes. The highest-impact R4-to-R6 breaks are the replacement of `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` by `reason: CodeableReference`, the reduction of `evaluationMessage` from repeating to single-valued, and the removal of `RequestGroup` as an allowed `result` target in favor of `RequestOrchestration` and many other request resources.

## Scope
This assessment covers local `GuidanceResponse` elements and local terminology bindings in the core package StructureDefinitions. Inherited `Resource` and `DomainResource` changes are out of scope and are not counted as findings.

## Main migration themes
R6 harmonizes several elements with newer workflow patterns: coded/reference reasons are modeled through `CodeableReference`, proposed actions are represented as a broader list of request-like resources, and more context fields are included in summaries. These changes improve expressiveness but require explicit migration rules for R4 data and for R6-to-R4 down-conversion.

## Highest-impact findings
The reason-field merge is a direct validation and codegen break for any R4 instances using `reasonCode` or `reasonReference`. `evaluationMessage` is also a direct validation break when more than one message is present. `result` is broader in R6, but R4 references to `RequestGroup` require a cross-version `RequestOrchestration` migration.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where transforms are not purely mechanical: pairing or splitting `CodeableReference` reasons, merging multiple `OperationOutcome` messages, choosing how to migrate `RequestGroup`, and deciding what to do with multiple R6 `result` references when down-converting.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some changes could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases or broader cardinality while adding preferred R6 elements. Those alternatives would have preserved R4 wire compatibility but at the cost of carrying legacy workflow patterns into R6.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should cover `DomainResource`/`Resource` inherited behavior, `CodeableReference`, and the `RequestGroup` to `RequestOrchestration` transition.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `GuidanceResponse` has local R4-to-R6 breaking changes despite retaining the same resource identity. The main concerns are the `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` merge into `reason`, `evaluationMessage` becoming single-valued, and `result` replacing `RequestGroup` with R6 request resources while also becoming repeatable. Confidence is high for the structural deltas; migration rationale would be improved by official diff notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on deterministic element transforms rather than whole-resource identity changes. `reasonCode` maps naturally to `reason.concept`, and `reasonReference` maps to `reason.reference`, but R6 can express paired concept/reference reasons and references outside the old R4 target set. `evaluationMessage` requires a policy for multiple messages. `result` requires both `RequestGroup` to `RequestOrchestration` handling and R6-to-R4 loss handling for multiple or newly allowed target resources.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present, complete, and directly comparable, and the required `guidance-response-status` CodeSystems are complete with identical code concepts. Confidence is lower only for inferred design intent and for precise operational migration guidance because no official diff, ballot rationale, or cross-version ConceptMap was supplied.

findings.title: R4 reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into R6 reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 represented coded reasons and referenced reasons as two separate repeating elements.

semanticText.definition: R4 used `reasonCode` for coded or textual reasons and `reasonReference` for references to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.

oldState.narrativeMd: `GuidanceResponse.reasonCode` was `0..* CodeableConcept`; `GuidanceResponse.reasonReference` was `0..* Reference(Condition | Observation | DiagnosticReport | DocumentReference)`.

newState.summary: R6 uses one repeating CodeableReference element for both concepts and references.

semanticText.definition: Describes the reason for the guidance response in coded or textual form, or indicates the reason the request was initiated.
semanticText.comment: R6 notes that references can point to any resource but are typically expected to refer to subject-specific data, and recommends targetElement/targetPath extensions for specificity.

newState.narrativeMd: `GuidanceResponse.reason` is `0..* CodeableReference`. Its contained `reference` has no target profile on the local element, so R6 can represent a broader reference domain than the R4 `reasonReference` target list.

facts.note: The old element names do not appear in the R6 GuidanceResponse snapshot.
The new element consolidates coded and referenced reasons.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `reason` short text matches the R4 reason elements, its definition combines both old definitions, and its `CodeableReference` type is specifically designed to carry either a concept or a resource reference.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break for any instance containing `reasonCode` or `reasonReference`, because those property names are no longer defined on the R6 resource. It is also a high runtime/codegen risk because generated R4 clients commonly expose two fields while R6 exposes one list of `CodeableReference`. R6-to-R4 conversion is not always lossless because an R6 `CodeableReference` can carry both a concept and a reference in one item, and the R6 local element does not restrict references to the four R4 target profiles.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reasons can be clinically or operationally important context for why decision support was invoked. Losing, mis-pairing, or over-broadening reason references can affect auditability and downstream review.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the R6 CodeableReference pattern for elements that may be either a coded concept or a concrete referenced resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases while adding `reason` as the preferred `CodeableReference` representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `CodeableReference` is a better R6 pattern for information that may be either coded or referential, and it avoids the artificial R4 split between `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`. The breakage is still significant because old property names disappear, but the best less-breaking base design has material long-term costs rather than being a clean substitute.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have kept `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated elements and added `reason` for the new `CodeableReference` pattern. That would let existing R4 instances validate with little or no transform. The cost is two overlapping ways to represent the same reason on the same resource; if both old and new fields appear, validators, search extractors, FHIRPath users, and converters need precedence and consistency rules, and deprecated representations may accumulate rather than disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve most R4 wire instances, but it creates duplicate same-resource representations, reconciliation rules, validation ambiguity, and a risk that legacy reason fields persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `GuidanceResponse.reasonReference` as `0..* Reference` constrained to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
R6 defines `GuidanceResponse.reason` as `0..* CodeableReference` and marks it summary.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are focused fragments. A normal R4-to-R6 transform can map each `reasonCode` item to one `reason.concept` item and each `reasonReference` item to one `reason.reference` item. Down-conversion from R6 may need to reject, split, or extend when an item carries both components or references a resource type outside the old R4 target list.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 collapses the two R4 reason arrays into one `reason` array of `CodeableReference`. This is a cleaner data model, but it breaks wire compatibility because R4 property names disappear. Systems that generated R4 classes, FHIRPath expressions, search extraction logic, or transforms around `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` must be updated to use nested `reason.concept` and `reason.reference`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with either `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because those elements are unknown in the R6 StructureDefinition. Conversely, an R6 instance can carry reason information that is not cleanly R4-representable, especially if the `CodeableReference` item has both a concept and reference or if the reference targets a resource outside Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, and DocumentReference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement an explicit transform: map R4 `reasonCode[n]` to R6 `reason[n].concept`, and map R4 `reasonReference[n]` to R6 `reason[n].reference`. Preserve both arrays, but do not invent pairing unless there is local business knowledge. For R6-to-R4, split simple concept-only and reference-only items, validate references against the R4 target set, and use an extension or manual review for paired or out-of-domain reasons.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably motivated by a better common representation for code-or-reference elements. It could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated old fields or by providing a formal cross-version extension. That alternative would reduce immediate migration cost but make the base resource carry two overlapping representations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether production validators enforce `CodeableReference.reference` target profiles when none are present on the local element. Also confirm whether any project-specific profile imposes a narrower R6 reason target set.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 instances that populate `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` need an explicit transform because R6 exposes one `reason` array of `CodeableReference` instead of the two old wire names. That is a real instance and generated-model break, and reverse conversion can require policy when an R6 item carries both a concept and a reference or references a resource outside the old R4 target set. The R6 design goal is still coherent: a single code-or-reference representation avoids the artificial R4 split, and the straightforward R4-to-R6 mapping is usually mechanical rather than expert-driven.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `GuidanceResponse.reason` is `0..* CodeableReference`; the old `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` element ids are absent.
R6 CodeableReference StructureDefinition: `concept` and `reference` are separate optional components.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral under the framework. They do not demand normative-level stability, but they also do not soften this the way FMM 0-1 would; the concrete wire/API mechanism drives the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` properties are not R6 GuidanceResponse elements. There is also runtime/API/codegen churn from two lists to one CodeableReference list and possible R6-to-R4 loss for paired or broader references.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could have retained deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` aliases while adding `reason`, preserving many R4 instances. The tradeoff is duplicate same-resource reason representations, conflict and precedence rules when old and new fields coexist, and prolonged support for the old split model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard break and a partial alias-style alternative, but the fresh review treats the CodeableReference consolidation as proportionate rather than a design issue needing renewed review.

findings.title: evaluationMessage maximum cardinality decreased from many to one

oldState.summary: R4 allowed zero or more evaluation message references.
oldState.narrativeMd: `GuidanceResponse.evaluationMessage` was a repeating reference to `OperationOutcome` in R4.

newState.summary: R6 allows at most one evaluation message reference.
newState.narrativeMd: `GuidanceResponse.evaluationMessage` remains a reference to `OperationOutcome`, but only one occurrence is allowed.

facts.note: The type and target are unchanged; only maximum cardinality narrowed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for R4 instances that contain more than one evaluation message. Runtime impact is medium because generated models may change from a list to a nullable singleton and because applications may have stored independent warnings or informational messages as separate `OperationOutcome` resources.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Evaluation messages can communicate warnings or informational diagnostics from a CDS engine. Dropping messages during migration can hide useful safety or operational context.

justification.inferredGoal: Limit a response to one aggregate OperationOutcome for evaluation diagnostics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `evaluationMessage` as `0..*` in the base resource and recommend one aggregate `OperationOutcome`, with profiles constraining to `0..1` where needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of encouraging one aggregate evaluation outcome is understandable, but the supplied evidence does not show why the base resource needed to prohibit multiple references. Reducing max cardinality from `*` to `1` is a direct hard break for existing R4 instances with repeated messages, and the same practical goal could have been pursued through guidance or profiles.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design would leave `GuidanceResponse.evaluationMessage` at `0..* Reference(OperationOutcome)` and update the definition to say producers should prefer a single aggregate `OperationOutcome` when possible. Implementations or IGs that need exactly one diagnostic bundle could constrain the element in a profile. This preserves R4 data while still steering R6 producers toward aggregation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alternative preserves all R4-valid repeated messages; the main tradeoff is slightly looser base uniformity and continued consumer responsibility for multiple diagnostics.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example assumes the two OperationOutcome resources are merged into one aggregate OperationOutcome. Whether that is safe depends on local provenance and issue-severity requirements.

findings.narrativeMd: `evaluationMessage` changed from repeating to single-valued. R4 producers could attach multiple separate evaluation outcomes, while R6 requires them to be represented through one reference. This is one of the clearest local validation breaks because no element rename or profile interpretation is needed to see the max-cardinality decrease.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with two or more `evaluationMessage` repetitions can validate in R4 but fail R6 cardinality validation. An R6-valid instance has at most one value, so R6-to-R4 representation is not a problem for this element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan R4 data for `evaluationMessage` arrays with more than one entry. Decide whether to merge multiple OperationOutcome resources, choose a primary message, preserve extra messages in extensions, or reject records for manual remediation. Tests should include zero, one, and multiple message cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrowing could have been avoided by keeping the R4 cardinality and adding guidance to aggregate messages. A strict base limit simplifies consumers but forces every migrator to solve aggregation or data loss for existing repeated messages.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: If historical data rarely used multiple evaluation messages, operational impact may be lower, but the structural break is unambiguous.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `evaluationMessage` is narrowed from repeating to single-valued while keeping the same OperationOutcome reference type. An R4 response with two diagnostic outcomes can be valid in R4 and fail R6 cardinality validation. If R6 wants one aggregate OperationOutcome, that goal could be met by guidance or profiling without prohibiting the existing base pattern, so the base max-cardinality reduction looks disproportionate.
keyEvidence: The element definition remains about messages resulting from evaluating the artifact or artifacts; the computable type and target are unchanged.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. They lower the stability expectation compared with normative content, but a direct cardinality break on evaluation diagnostics with a low-cost less-breaking design still warrants renewed review.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with more than one `evaluationMessage` repetition exceed the R6 maximum of one. Runtime/API/codegen also changes from list handling to a nullable singleton.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: keep the base element `0..*` and recommend that producers use one aggregate OperationOutcome where practical, with profiles constraining to `0..1` for ecosystems that require it. This preserves R4 data and still supports the apparent simplification goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high impact and less-breaking-alternative-available assessment match the fresh path-level review.

findings.title: result targets changed from CarePlan or RequestGroup to a broad R6 request-resource set

oldState.summary: R4 result referenced at most one CarePlan or RequestGroup.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 target set was narrow: `CarePlan` or `RequestGroup`.

newState.summary: R6 result references zero or more proposed actions across many request-like resources, including RequestOrchestration instead of RequestGroup.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 retains `CarePlan`, replaces the R4 `RequestGroup` target with `RequestOrchestration`, and adds many other request-resource targets.

facts.newValue: StructureDefinition-RequestOrchestration.json present in R6 package; StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json not present in R6 package
facts.note: This supports a likely RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration migration dependency.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances whose `result` points to a `RequestGroup` are no longer valid against the R6 target set without migrating the referenced resource to `RequestOrchestration`. R6 can also point `result` at many resource types that the R4 base definition does not allow. Runtime risk is high for generated references, switch statements, resource loaders, and downstream CDS workflows that assumed only `CarePlan` or `RequestGroup`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `result` carries proposed actions from decision support. Incorrect target migration can change or hide actionable recommendations.

justification.inferredGoal: Align GuidanceResponse proposed actions with the broader R6 request-resource model and the RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration transition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a legacy `RequestGroup` target, or loosen target profiling enough for legacy references, while adding `RequestOrchestration` and the broader R6 request target set.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: `result` represents proposed actions, and the broader target list plus `RequestOrchestration` aligns the resource with the R6 request model. A less-breaking design is imaginable, but it depends on cross-artifact legacy support for `RequestGroup` or on less precise target constraints; ordinary conversion guidance alone would not be a base-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The least disruptive base design would have allowed `RequestGroup` as a deprecated legacy target if R6 also retained a compatible `RequestGroup` definition or profile. Another possible design would make `result` target profiling broader so old `RequestGroup/...` references are not rejected by the `GuidanceResponse` element itself. Both alternatives have material costs: they either keep a replaced workflow resource alive in the core model or reduce the value of target-profile validation for proposed actions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This only partially solves compatibility because it requires retaining an obsolete or compatibility-only target, or weakens target validation and creates RequestGroup/RequestOrchestration interoperability burden.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are CarePlan and RequestGroup.
R6 target profiles include CarePlan, RequestOrchestration, and many other request resources, but not RequestGroup.
The R4 package contains StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json; the R6 package contains StructureDefinition-RequestOrchestration.json and no StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is valid only if the referenced RequestGroup resource also conforms to R4. The R6 migration example assumes the referenced resource itself has been migrated to RequestOrchestration.

findings.narrativeMd: `result` no longer means only a `CarePlan` or `RequestGroup`. R6 broadens it to many request-like targets and uses `RequestOrchestration` in place of `RequestGroup`. This affects validation, generated type unions, and application logic that dispatches proposed actions by resource type.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `result.reference` pointing to `RequestGroup/...` can become invalid in R6 because `RequestGroup` is not in the R6 target profile list. Conversely, an R6 instance whose result points to MedicationRequest, ServiceRequest, Task, or other newly allowed targets is not valid against the R4 base target list.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migrate referenced `RequestGroup` resources to `RequestOrchestration` before or alongside the GuidanceResponse transform, and update `result.reference` values accordingly. For R6-to-R4, allow only CarePlan and successfully mapped RequestOrchestration-to-RequestGroup references; otherwise preserve data in an extension or reject for manual handling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader target set is useful because decision support can propose many kinds of actions. It was not fully backward compatible because one of the two R4 targets disappeared. A compatibility target or formal cross-version mapping would reduce migration ambiguity but would also keep legacy workflow concepts in the base resource.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Treat this finding together with the separate resource-level analysis of `RequestGroup` and `RequestOrchestration`; this report does not validate the internal element mapping between those resources.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `result` still carries proposed actions, but the allowed target set changes substantially: `CarePlan` is retained, `RequestGroup` is no longer an R6 target, and many R6 request resources including `RequestOrchestration` are added. R4 data pointing to RequestGroup needs coordinated migration of the referenced resource, and R6 data can point to action resources that R4 never allowed. The break is meaningful because proposed actions can be clinically important, but it appears tied to the broader R6 workflow model rather than a simple avoidable rename.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `GuidanceResponse.result` targets `CarePlan`, `RequestOrchestration`, and multiple other request-like resources, but not `RequestGroup`.
Local packages: R4 contains `StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json`; R6 contains `StructureDefinition-RequestOrchestration.json` and no `StructureDefinition-RequestGroup.json`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. The judgment depends on the action-reference migration burden and safety relevance, not on a strong stability guarantee.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: under target-profile/resource-type validation, an R4 `result` reference to `RequestGroup/...` no longer conforms in R6. There is also runtime/API/codegen risk for changed target unions and R6-to-R4 loss for newly allowed target resources.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could have retained a legacy `RequestGroup` target or made the target profile looser. That would preserve more R4 references, but it either keeps an obsolete workflow resource in play or weakens validation of proposed-action targets, so it is not a clearly low-cost base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly flags high migration risk and only a partial alternative, but the fresh review treats the change as proportionate to the RequestGroup-to-RequestOrchestration transition.

findings.title: result changed from single-valued to repeating

oldState.summary: R4 allowed at most one result reference.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 clients could model `result` as a singleton optional reference.

newState.summary: R6 allows zero or more result references.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 clients must model `result` as a collection, even if many instances still contain only one result.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Increasing a maximum cardinality does not make old R4 instances invalid in R6, but it changes generated APIs from singleton to list and creates a high R6-to-R4 representability risk. An R6 GuidanceResponse with multiple result references cannot be represented in the R4 base element without dropping, choosing, bundling, or extending.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Multiple proposed actions may all be clinically relevant. Losing all but one action in down-conversion can materially change the decision-support recommendation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow one GuidanceResponse to return multiple proposed actions directly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: increasing `result` max from `1` to `*` preserves R4-valid cardinalities; the concern is R6-to-R4 round-trip and generated API shape.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple result references is consistent with a GuidanceResponse producing multiple proposed actions, and it does not make any R4-valid instance invalid in R6 on cardinality grounds. The compatibility concern is real for scalar-to-list APIs and R6-to-R4 conversion, but it is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue for existing instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable in the R4-to-R6 instance-validation sense because every absent or singleton R4 `result` still fits R6 `0..*`. A singleton-plus-aggregation design could avoid R6-to-R4 loss and scalar/list code changes, but it would fail or dilute the R6 expressiveness goal and should be treated as a conversion policy tradeoff rather than an R4-preserving base alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping a singleton would preserve old codegen and down-conversion expectations, but it would block or obscure the R6 goal of directly returning multiple proposed actions.

examples.examplesMd: Even if both referenced resources could be individually represented in R4, the base R4 `GuidanceResponse.result` slot can carry only one reference.

findings.narrativeMd: `result` became repeating. This is not an old-instance validation break, but it is a meaningful representation change for code generators and for down-converters. R4 code that treats `result` as a scalar must be rewritten to handle zero, one, or many R6 references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is safe for cardinality because any R4 singleton fits within R6 `0..*`. R6-to-R4 is not safe when more than one result appears; a strict R4 validator will reject repeated `result` values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and serializers to treat R6 `result` as an array. For R6-to-R4, define a business rule: select one primary result, wrap multiple actions into a mappable orchestration resource, store extras in extensions, or reject the instance for manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 choice improves expressiveness but sacrifices direct R4 round-tripping. A backward-compatible alternative would be to keep a singleton and require aggregation, but that would make the R6 base less direct for multi-action guidance.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Changing `result` from optional singleton to repeating does not invalidate any R4 GuidanceResponse by itself, but it is still a real model-shape change for R6 code and a direct loss point for R6-to-R4 conversion when multiple proposed actions are present. Because GuidanceResponse can naturally produce more than one action, the R6 expressiveness goal is reasonable and the singleton-preserving alternative would mainly push aggregation complexity elsewhere.
keyEvidence: The element definition in both versions describes actions produced by evaluating the artifact.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. The lack of an old-valid/new-invalid cardinality break weighs against Revisit, while the generated API and reverse-conversion impact prevents dismissing it entirely.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated R6 models and application logic must treat `result` as a collection rather than a singleton. R6-to-R4 loss occurs when more than one result reference must be down-converted into the R4 single slot.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for preserving R4-valid instances, because every R4 absent-or-singleton value fits R6 `0..*`. Keeping R6 singleton would reduce API churn and reverse loss, but it would not meet the R6 goal of directly carrying multiple proposed actions.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report appropriately treats this as not a hard R4-to-R6 instance break but as meaningful runtime and R6-to-R4 migration risk.

findings.title: R6 adds optional GuidanceResponse.location

oldState.summary: No local `location` element existed on R4 GuidanceResponse.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has no base element for the principal physical location where the guidance response occurred.

newState.summary: R6 adds `location` as an optional Reference(Location), included in summaries.

semanticText.definition: The principal physical location where the guidance response was performed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can now carry location context directly on the base resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element is optional, so it does not invalidate R4 instances when moving to R6. It is still a representability risk for down-conversion because R4 has no base slot for this location. R6 clients and generated models also gain a new property that summary serializers may include.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Location can influence audit, workflow, or access-control decisions, but the element is optional and not a modifier.

justification.inferredGoal: Add explicit event-location context to GuidanceResponse.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `location` is an optional R6 addition, so it does not invalidate R4 instances; R4 extension mapping is a down-conversion mitigation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional event-location context is a reasonable and forward-compatible way to increase R6 expressiveness. Because the element is `0..1`, existing R4 GuidanceResponse instances are not made invalid by the base R6 design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. An R4 extension can preserve populated R6 `location` during down-conversion, but that is an extension/backport mitigation rather than evidence of a different backward-compatible R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is for R6-to-R4 round-trips only: R4 needs an extension or accepts loss of populated location context.

evidence.detail: No `GuidanceResponse.location` element is present in the R4 snapshot.
R6 defines `GuidanceResponse.location` as `0..1 Reference(Location)` and summary.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 field can be preserved in R4 only by an extension or external association; R4 has no built-in `GuidanceResponse.location` element.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds an optional `location` element for the principal physical location where the guidance response was performed. Optional additions are forward-compatible for R4 data, but they create round-trip risk for R6 data that must be stored or transmitted as R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this change because no new required element was added. R6 instances that populate `location` cannot be represented in core R4 GuidanceResponse without an extension; strict R4 parsers will reject a raw `location` property.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, no action is required unless location can be derived and should be populated. For R6-to-R4, define a cross-version extension or omit with documented data loss. Include access-control and audit workflows in tests if they use location context.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding an optional element is the least disruptive base-resource change in the forward direction. The unavoidable backward-compatibility issue is that R4 cannot carry new R6 fields without extensions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `location` as `0..1 Reference(Location)`. This is forward-compatible for R4 data because no existing instance is required to add it and no old field is removed. A populated R6 location has no core R4 slot on down-conversion, but that is the ordinary cost of an optional new field rather than a standards-design concern for R4-to-R6 compatibility.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: no `GuidanceResponse.location` element is present.
R6 StructureDefinition: `GuidanceResponse.location` is `0..1 Reference(Location)` and is marked summary.
The new element is not a modifier and has minimum cardinality zero.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. Because the change is optional and additive, FMM does not raise it to a compatibility problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: a populated R6 `location` cannot be represented in core R4 GuidanceResponse without an extension or external association. There is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable: the base R6 design is already the compatibility-preserving form for forward migration, an optional addition. R4 extensions can mitigate reverse conversion but are not a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing evidence and reverse-conversion note are correct, but the fresh review rates the optional additive change as no problem rather than a material medium-impact concern.

findings.title: subject, encounter, and occurrenceDateTime are newly included in summaries

oldState.summary: These three context elements were not marked summary in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 snapshots show `isSummary` false or absent for `subject`, `encounter`, and `occurrenceDateTime`.

newState.summary: These three context elements are marked summary in R6.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 marks `subject`, `encounter`, and `occurrenceDateTime` with `isSummary: true`, so they are part of summary representations.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flags do not affect whether a full instance validates. They can affect `_summary` REST responses, summary serialization, generated lightweight models, indexing, and privacy review because more context may be included in summary views.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The newly summarized fields are contextual and may affect access-control or minimal-response behavior, but they are not modifiers and do not change core validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose key subject, encounter, and timing context in summary representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 summary flags unchanged and rely on `_elements`, profiles, or implementation guidance for clients that need subject, encounter, and timing context.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The newly summarized fields are important context for a GuidanceResponse, so including them in R6 summaries is understandable and does not affect full-resource instance validity. The less-breaking design would avoid runtime surprises for clients with strict summary-payload expectations, but it would weaken the usefulness of the standard summary view.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `subject`, `encounter`, and `occurrenceDateTime` out of the summary set and documented that clients should request them explicitly with `_elements` or use profiles/IG guidance. That avoids changing default summary payload shape, but it does not fully meet the same R6 goal of making key context available in normal summary representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves exact R4 summary payload expectations, but only partially meets the R6 goal because the context would not appear in default summary responses.

evidence.detail: R4 marks these local elements as not summary.
R6 marks all three local elements as summary.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed because summary flags change server/client summary behavior, not full-resource validation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 summary views include more GuidanceResponse context than R4. This may be welcome, but it can surprise clients that use summary responses for small payloads, redaction, or lightweight indexing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Full R4 and R6 instances are not made valid or invalid by this flag change. The compatibility effect is runtime behavior: summary serializers and `_summary=true` responses may include fields that were not summary in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review clients and tests that compare exact summary payloads. If summaries are used for privacy or minimal-disclosure workflows, confirm that adding subject, encounter, and occurrenceDateTime is acceptable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is a behavioral representation change rather than an instance-schema break. A backward-compatible alternative would be to leave summaries unchanged and require clients to request these fields explicitly, but that reduces the usefulness of the default summary.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 marks `subject`, `encounter`, and `occurrenceDateTime` as summary elements while leaving their cardinalities and types compatible. This can change `_summary` responses or generated summary views, so clients with exact payload or privacy assumptions should notice it. It does not affect full-resource validity and the added fields are ordinary context rather than modifiers.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `GuidanceResponse.subject`, `encounter`, and `occurrenceDateTime` are not summary elements.
R6 StructureDefinition: the same three elements have `isSummary: true`.
The three elements keep the same cardinalities and datatypes/reference targets across R4 and R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral. Since this is a summary representation flag change rather than a validation break, maturity context does not make it a Revisit issue.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: summary serializers and `_summary` responses may include more context fields. There is no old-valid/new-invalid instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial but not compelling: keeping the R4 summary flags would preserve exact summary payload expectations, but it would also make the standard R6 summary less useful for subject, encounter, and timing context.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing low-impact framing is consistent with the fresh review.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. Maturity/status changed and is recorded as a non-breaking notable change.
No local minimum cardinality increased. Material maximum-cardinality changes are reported for `evaluationMessage` and `result`; other local cardinalities are unchanged.

`requestIdentifier`, `identifier`, `module[x]`, `status`, `subject`, `encounter`, `occurrenceDateTime`, `performer`, `note`, `outputParameters`, and `dataRequirement` retain their local types. The material `reason` model change is reported separately.
`subject`, `encounter`, `performer`, `evaluationMessage`, and `outputParameters` retain their reference targets. `result` and new `location` target behavior are reported separately.
`status` remains required against GuidanceResponse Status, and the complete local R4/R6 CodeSystems list the same six codes. `module[x]` gains only an example binding, recorded as non-breaking.
No local GuidanceResponse-specific invariant was added or removed. Changes to `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension-related constraints are inherited from base artifacts and excluded from findings.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value was found on the compared GuidanceResponse elements.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were found.
`GuidanceResponse.status` remains a modifier with the same local modifier reason. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.
No local slicing or slice definitions were found on GuidanceResponse in either version.

The resource type name and canonical identity did not change. Serialization/codegen risks are limited to renamed/merged fields, cardinality shape changes, new fields, and summary flag changes reported above.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact moved from draft/trial-use metadata to active/normative metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The resource identity and element wire format are not changed by the metadata status alone.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The normative status may increase expectations that future R6 changes remain stable. It also changes conformance messaging and documentation, but not instance validation for existing element content.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: module[x] gains an example Guidance Module Code binding
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength is `example`, so conformant instances are not required to draw codes from the new value set. The choice types and cardinality are unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or validators that incorrectly enforce example bindings could create false positives. Correct FHIR validation should treat the new binding as advisory.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: GuidanceResponse.status binding version changes but codes remain stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 and R6 complete CodeSystems for `http://hl7.org/fhir/guidance-response-status` both contain `success`, `data-requested`, `data-required`, `in-progress`, `failure`, and `entered-in-error` with the same definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that pin the canonical with a version suffix must update from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`, but no code remapping was identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several definitions and requirements were clarified without changing local validation domains
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `identifier`, `subject`, and `encounter` have expanded definitions, comments, or requirements in R6, but their local cardinalities, datatypes, and reference target sets remain compatible.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review business rules that interpreted `subject` as only a patient. R4 already allowed Group, and R6 clarifies this as an individual or set of individuals.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `GuidanceResponse.result` migration depends on how R4 `RequestGroup` maps to R6 `RequestOrchestration`, including reference rewriting and internal action semantics.
`GuidanceResponse.reason` uses R6 `CodeableReference`; exact round-trip behavior depends on datatype semantics and any cross-version conventions for pairing `concept` and `reference`.

Several inherited snapshot differences, such as base constraints, `Resource.language` binding, and `DomainResource.modifierExtension` summary behavior, are excluded here and should be handled by base-artifact reports.
Search parameters were explicitly out of scope. R6 local element renames and additions may affect search behavior, especially for reason, result, location, and status.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot rationale was used. Structural confidence is high, but justification and backward-compatible alternative assessments are partly inferred.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official version-to-version diff, ballot reconciliation notes, or change proposals for GuidanceResponse.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local complete CodeSystem resources for the required status binding and did not call a terminology server. This is sufficient for visible code equality but not for external expansion behavior.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run R4 and R6 terminology expansions using the intended terminology server and version pinning policy.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No production corpus or implementation-guide profiles were reviewed, so expected prevalence is estimated from element purpose rather than observed data.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Profile and corpus analysis could quantify how often multiple evaluation messages, RequestGroup results, multiple results, or reason fields appear.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The report identifies `RequestGroup` to `RequestOrchestration` and `CodeableReference` dependencies but does not perform full element-by-element conversion analysis for those separate artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use dedicated reports or ConceptMaps for `CodeableReference`, `RequestGroup`, and `RequestOrchestration`.
